title: The DP-added H and C dependencies of RWB-P7-E2042-APP are absent from the metadata rows
source: Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 R5.5 and R5.7; _work/msr/wp/B-P7-05.md story line RWB-P7-E2042-APP
description: The metadata names Depends on (build) None and Contract dependencies RWB-P3-E2042-CON only, while the DP table adds eight platform H dependencies and three C dependencies: H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1072-CON, RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON, and C RWB-P7-E1073-CON, RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON.
evidence: Template and Rules R5.5 rows DP-03, DP-04, DP-06, DP-07, DP-10, DP-14, DP-15 and DP-19; the same pattern in the sibling stories RWB-P3-E2042-APP and RWB-P7-E2027-APP, which also omit the DP-added rows from the metadata.
proposed: Keep the metadata as written and carry the DP-added dependencies in the story: they are platform wave-0 contracts and published contracts built against as fakes, so none blocks the build and Ready to start stays Day 1 (R5.7 rule 2).

title: PAYMENT_MATCH is labelled PMT-2026.12 from 2026-12-15 in this key and PM-2026.12 from 2026-12-01 in RWB-E2-027
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 042 Epic 2 rule packages in Drools v1.md section 3; the RWB-E2-027 lineage as carried by RWB-P7-E2027-APP and RWB-P7-E2042-APP
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria AC3; 13 Solution plan
description: This legacy key agrees the label PMT-2026.12 with valid from 2026-12-15 for the PAYMENT_MATCH package. The RWB-E2-027 lineage agrees PM-2026.12 with valid from 2026-12-01 for the same package code. Both values are copied from their source stories, so the registry would hold two labels and two valid-from dates for one package.
evidence: RWB E2 042 section 3: 'The version labels are agreed on 16 November 2026: "RES-2026.12", "PMT-2026.12" and "BKG-2026.12", all valid from 2026-12-15 (assumed)'. RWB-P7-E2027-APP section 3 and 13: '"PM-2026.12" is in force from 2026-12-01' and the note that RWB-P3-E2042-APP and RWB-P7-E2042-APP hold the same package under PMT-2026.12 from 2026-12-15.
proposed: Do not choose silently. This story copies the legacy value of its own key (PMT-2026.12, valid from 2026-12-15) and raises one reconciliation with the owner of RWB-E2-027 so that one package code holds one version row before SIT.

title: The decision code of a rule-governance entry is not named in any source this key may read
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P7 Decision center and log v2.md T3.1 and T3.2; FSD P7 v3 A2.7
description: decision_log_entry carries decision_code (DF-DEC-003) from the LOV-DECISION list, but the value a load, an approval, a promotion or a rollback writes is not given. The legacy story adds no decision code, and TSD P7 v2 T3.2 lists the version states and other LOVs but not the LOV-DECISION values.
evidence: TSD P7 v2 T3.1 decision_log_entry DF-DEC-003 decision_code LOV, list LOV-DECISION; TSD P7 v2 T3.2 lists LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL, LOV-APPROVAL-STATUS, LOV-CAPABILITY and LOV-PRODUCT only; FSD P7 v3 A2.7 names no governance decision code.
proposed: Resolve the code from LOV-DECISION at run time through DP-07 and write no literal in the story or the code; confirm the value with the LOV-DECISION owner before SIT.

title: The name of the rwb-decision database login is not specified
source: Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 R4 and R5.5 DP-02
description: DP-02 requires one login per service and the service table names a login per service, but the login name of rwb-decision is not written in the sources this key may read. The legacy story uses the shared monolith login, which must not appear in the target.
evidence: Template and Rules R4 ('login per service') and R5.5 DP-02 ('One login per service'); the Architecture v5 extract names the schema rwb_decision and the grants model but not the login string.
proposed: Write the login only as 'the rwb-decision login (DP-02)' and leave the name to the platform DB story that creates the login and the grants.

title: The detail text of MSG-P3-027 for the two Epic 2 checks is not fixed
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 042 Epic 2 rule packages in Drools v1.md sections 5 and 14; FSD P7 v3 A2.7
description: MSG-P3-027 is 'The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}.' The legacy story says the match order and the catalog completeness are part of the schema check, but it does not fix the {detail} wording for those two checks, so two implementations could name different cells, rule IDs or columns for the same refusal.
evidence: Legacy section 14: 'For MSG-P3-027 the {check} value is compile, schema, overlap, unreachable row, default row or scenario; the match order and the catalog completeness are part of the schema check. The {detail} names row IDs, cells or scenario IDs only'; FSD P7 v3 A2.7 AC-EXC-P7-007-02 uses 'the schema check naming row 9 and its column'.
proposed: Fix the detail to rule IDs, row orders and column names only, with no case fact and no person, and confirm the exact text with the business analyst before SIT.

title: The four rule registry tables are declared for P4 and P3 in their TSDs and are absent from the P7 TSD
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P7 Decision center and log v2.md T3.1; TSD P4 v3 T3.1; TSD P3 v3 T3.1; Architecture v5 slides 27 and 41; Ownership Map v1
description: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 declares rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case for P4, TSD P3 v3 declares the same family for P3, and TSD P7 v2 T3.1 defines only decision_log_entry and approval. Architecture v5 slides 27 and 41 and the R-PREC default ruling put the registry in P7, so the registry of this story sits in a schema whose own TSD does not describe its tables.
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 'rule_package (NEW)' and the three companion tables; TSD P3 v3 T3.1 rule tables; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 lists decision_log_entry and approval; Arch v5 slide 41 'P7 rwb-decision | approvals, central decision ledger, DMN model registry'; Ownership Map v1 rule_package owner P7 with ruling ASM-A6-tables-3.
proposed: Read the R-PREC default ruling as P7: this story owns the four tables in rwb_decision and the P3 and P4 declarations are not built. Record the reading and ask the P7 TSD to add the tables at its next version.

title: The package title, the dry-run breakdown, the MSG-P3-015 text and the switch-off answer are not specified
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 042 Epic 2 rule packages in Drools v1.md; FSD P7 v3 A2.7; TSD P7 v2 T3.1
section: 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 and AC4; 11 Data; 13 Solution plan; 14 Validation and messages
description: Several values used by this story have no source: the title text of each package row (DF-REF-276), the breakdown of dry_run_counts (DF-REF-293), the text of MSG-P3-015, the body of the rollback answer beyond the two version states, and the answer of the three admin operations when the legacy flag is off.
evidence: The legacy story names DF-REF-276 and DF-REF-293 and defers the checklist to RWB-E2-041, but gives no title, no count and no rollback answer; FSD P7 v3 AC-EXC-P7-007-05 names MSG-P3-015 without its text; the flag behaviour is described only as '404 or NoPackageInForce' in the legacy section 13.
proposed: Write the placeholder at each point and use the defaults of ASM-B-P7-05-E2042-7; the tests assert presence and stability, never an invented business number.

title: The BRD section pointers copied from the legacy story no longer match BRD v2 and v4
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epic 1 v4; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epic 2 v2; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4; legacy RWB-E2-042 section 18
description: The legacy story cites 'Epic 1, 3.3; Epic 2, 3.2 and 3.8; Program, 5.3' for REQ-CWC-013 and REQ-CWC-014. In BRD Epic 1 v4, section 3.3 is P3 Case and workflow and the requirement set sits in section 4; in BRD Epic 2 v2, section 3.2 is P2 Integration, 3.7 is P7 and 3.8 is P8 Payments; Program v4 section 5.3 carries the requirement set.
evidence: Business Requirements Epic 1 v4 headings 3.1 to 3.9 and line 221 where REQ-CWC-013 sits in section 4; Business Requirements Epic 2 v2 headings 3.1 to 3.10; Business Requirements Program v4 line 160.
proposed: Cite Epic 1 section 4 and Program section 5.3 in the traceability table, keep the requirement IDs and the requirement text unchanged, and note the stale legacy pointer rather than deleting it.
